jungle.name: Jungle World
jungle.blurb: Hot, green and full of trees

night.name: Night World
night.blurb: Friends who wake up at night

sunny.name: Sunny the Capybara
sunny.home: rivers and lakes of South America

activity.morning: Sunny munches juicy pond grass by the sunny lake. The frogs sing a morning song, and a brave little bird lands on her back. Tickle, tickle! Up in the sky, puffy popcorn clouds float by. Rain is coming!
activity.afternoon: It’s getting hot! Sunny finds a cool, squishy mud puddle, all for herself. She closes her eyes and takes a nap. Plip, plop! Raindrops land on her nose. Nap over — and now she’s hungry again!
activity.evening: Under the big, bright moon, Sunny’s family munches together. Then — WHISTLE! Danger! Crocs are near! Clever Sunny leads everyone to hide in the mud. The crocs swim past. Safe! Goodnight, Sunny.

facts: Capybaras are the biggest rodents in the world!
Capybaras can bark like a dog, purr when they’re happy, and whistle to call their family.
Rolling in mud keeps capybaras cool, protects their skin from the sun and chases away bugs!
Capybaras love big families, with lots of cousins and friends.

echo.name: Echo the Hippo

activity.morning: Echo the Hippo wakes up in the cool river. Only her eyes, ears and nose peek out of the water. Peek-a-boo!
activity.afternoon: Hippos don’t really swim — Echo walks and bounces along the bottom of the river. Boing, boing, boing!
activity.evening: When the sun goes down, Echo climbs out of the water to munch grass all night long. Munch, munch. Goodnight, Echo!

facts: Hippos spend most of the day in water to keep their skin cool.
Hippos can close their ears and nose when they go under water!
Hippos come out at night to eat grass.

click.name: Click the Tokay Gecko
click.home: trees and houses of Southeast Asia

activity.morning: Click the Tokay Gecko is sleepy. Geckos like Click rest in the daytime, hiding in a cozy crack in a big tree.
activity.afternoon: Click wakes up a little and licks his big orange eye to clean it. Tokay geckos have no moving eyelids to blink!
activity.evening: Night time is Click’s time! “To-kay! To-kay!” he calls, and climbs up the tree to look for crunchy bugs. Goodnight, Click!

facts: Tokay geckos are named after their loud call: “To-kay!”
Tokay geckos can climb walls and even walk upside down with their special toes!
Tokay geckos clean their eyes by licking them.

cat.name: Mimi the Cat

activity.morning: The sun tickles Mimi’s nose. She stretches her front paws… then her back paws… then she yawns a BIG yawn. Breakfast time!
activity.afternoon: Mimi finds a ball of red wool. Roll, pounce, roll, pounce! Oh no — now she’s all tangled up!
activity.evening: Mimi curls into a soft, round ball on the warm blanket. Purr… purr… Goodnight, Mimi.

facts: Cats often purr when they are relaxed, but they can also purr when worried or unwell.
Cats sleep for most of the day!

dog.name: Bruno the Dog

activity.morning: Bruno wags his tail so fast his whole body wiggles. He brings his leash: “Walk? Walk? Walk?”
activity.afternoon: In the park Bruno digs a hole, finds a stick and gets mud on his nose. Splash — bath time!
activity.evening: Bruno lies by the door with his favourite sock. Snore… Goodnight, Bruno.

facts: Dogs use their very sensitive noses to discover scents that people cannot notice!
Dogs wag their tails to show how they feel.

cow.name: Rosa the Cow

activity.morning: Rosa opens one eye, then the other. The grass is wet and shiny. Munch, munch!
activity.afternoon: Rosa swishes her tail at a buzzing fly. Swish! Swish! Go away, fly!
activity.evening: The sky turns pink. Rosa walks back to the warm barn. Moo… Goodnight, Rosa.

facts: Cows have best friends and feel calmer when they are together.

duck.name: Pippo the Duck

activity.morning: Pippo waddles out of his nest. Left foot, right foot — SPLASH! Into the pond.
activity.afternoon: Pippo dives: bottom up, head down! Bubbles everywhere!
activity.evening: Pippo tucks his head under his soft wing. Quack… Goodnight, Pippo.

facts: Ducks have water-resistant feathers that help keep their skin warm and dry!

orangutan.name: Oli the Orangutan
orangutan.home: rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra, in Asia

activity.morning: Oli wakes up in a leafy nest, high, high up in the trees. Good morning, jungle!
activity.afternoon: Oli swings from branch to branch, looking for juicy fruit. Uh-oh, rain! Oli holds a big leaf like an umbrella.
activity.evening: Oli bends soft branches into a brand-new bed for the night. Goodnight, Oli!

facts: Orangutans usually build a fresh nest in the trees each night, and sometimes reuse one.
An orangutan’s arms are longer than its legs — perfect for swinging.

tiger.name: Tiko the Tiger

activity.morning: Tiko stretches a long, long stretch and licks a big striped paw.
activity.afternoon: It’s hot! Tiko jumps into the river. Splash! Unlike many other cats, tigers are strong swimmers!
activity.evening: Tiko walks quietly through the shadows. The stripes make Tiko almost invisible. Goodnight, Tiko!

facts: No two tigers have the same stripes!
Tigers love to swim — unlike most cats.

toucan.name: Kiki the Toucan

activity.morning: Kiki shakes her big, colourful beak and sings to the sunrise.
activity.afternoon: Kiki picks a berry, throws it up in the air… and catches it! Gulp!
activity.evening: Kiki turns her head, rests her beak on her back and folds her tail over like a blanket. Goodnight, Kiki!

facts: A toucan’s big beak is very light — it’s full of tiny air spaces inside!
Toucans sleep with their beak on their back and their tail folded over it.

elephant.name: Ella the Elephant

activity.morning: Ella fills her trunk at the waterhole and — WHOOSH! — gives herself a cool shower.
activity.afternoon: Ella throws dust and mud on her back. It’s like sunscreen for elephants!
activity.evening: Ella’s family walks home together, following the wise grandma elephant. Goodnight, Ella!

facts: An elephant uses its flexible trunk to pick up tiny leaves and move heavy branches!
Elephant family groups are often led by an experienced older female.

giraffe.name: Zuri the Giraffe

activity.morning: Zuri stretches her long neck to the very top of the tree. The best leaves are up here!
activity.afternoon: Thirsty! Zuri spreads her long legs wide, wide, wide to reach the water.
activity.evening: The stars come out. Zuri hums a soft, low hum. Goodnight, Zuri!

facts: Giraffes are the tallest living land animals!
A giraffe has a long, often dark-coloured tongue that helps it grasp leaves.

zebra.name: Ziggy the Zebra

activity.morning: Ziggy and the herd munch fresh grass in the morning sun.
activity.afternoon: Ziggy and a friend nibble each other’s necks. Scratch, scratch — that’s how zebras say “I like you”!
activity.evening: The herd stays close together. Some zebras keep watch while the others rest. Goodnight, Ziggy!

facts: Every zebra has its own stripe pattern, like a fingerprint!
Zebras are cousins of horses.

turtle.name: Tuga the Sea Turtle
turtle.home: warm seas all over the world

activity.morning: Tuga swims up, up, up to the top of the water and takes a big breath of air.
activity.afternoon: Tuga is a green sea turtle. She munches soft seagrass on the sea floor. Yum!
activity.evening: Tuga rests under a rocky ledge as the sea turns dark. Goodnight, Tuga!

facts: Sea turtles breathe air, so they swim to the top to take a breath. Adult green sea turtles mainly eat algae and seagrass.
Baby sea turtles hatch on the beach and race to the sea!

octopus.name: Inky the Octopus

activity.morning: Inky wakes up and changes from pale to dark and mottled! Good morning, colours!
activity.afternoon: Inky squeezes through a tiny hole. Octopuses have no bones, but their hard beak must fit through the opening!
activity.evening: Inky curls up in a cozy den made of shells. Goodnight, Inky!

facts: An octopus has eight arms and three hearts!
Octopuses can change colour in a blink.

dolphin.name: Fin the Dolphin

activity.morning: Fin jumps high out of the waves. Splash!
activity.afternoon: Fin whistles to the family. Bottlenose dolphins can have their own special whistle — a little like saying their name!
activity.evening: Fin sleeps with half of the brain at a time, so one eye stays a little open. Goodnight, Fin!

facts: Bottlenose dolphins have their own special whistles — a little like names!
Dolphins sleep with half of their brain at a time.

penguin.name: Pingo the Penguin

activity.morning: Pingo waddles across the ice. Waddle, waddle, waddle!
activity.afternoon: Pingo flops on the belly and slides down the snow. Wheee!
activity.evening: Brrr, it’s cold! All the penguins huddle together to stay warm. Goodnight, Pingo!

facts: Penguins can’t fly, but they are super swimmers!
Emperor penguin dads keep the egg warm on their feet!

polarbear.name: Nanu the Polar Bear
polarbear.home: the snow and sea ice of the Arctic

activity.morning: Nanu rolls and rubs in the fresh snow to clean the thick white fur.
activity.afternoon: Nanu swims from one piece of ice to the next. Paddle, paddle!
activity.evening: Nanu curls up in the snow, nose under paw. Goodnight, Nanu!

facts: Under its white fur, a polar bear’s skin is black!
Polar bears are great swimmers.

seal.name: Sami the Seal
seal.home: the icy seas of the Arctic

activity.morning: Sami pops up through a hole in the ice. Peek-a-boo!
activity.afternoon: Sami dives deep, deep down to look for fish. Hold your breath!
activity.evening: Sami rests on the ice under the dancing northern lights. Goodnight, Sami!

facts: Seals are mammals. They breathe air and can stay underwater for a long time.
Baby harp seals are born with fluffy white fur.

bear.name: Bo the Bear
bear.home: forests and mountains of Europe and North America

activity.morning: Bo stands in the river and — SPLASH! — catches a fish.
activity.afternoon: Bo finds a bush full of sweet berries. Munch, munch, munch!
activity.evening: Bo’s tummy is full and Bo is sleepy. Soon it will be winter — time for the long sleep in a cozy den. Goodnight, Bo!

facts: Many brown bears spend the coldest months resting in a den.
Brown bears eat many different foods, including berries, plants, insects and fish.

squirrel.name: Hazel the Squirrel

activity.morning: Hazel runs up the tree trunk — zip, zip, zip!
activity.afternoon: Hazel buries nuts in the ground to eat later. One here… one there…
activity.evening: Hazel curls up in a round nest of twigs and moss, her bushy tail like a blanket. Goodnight, Hazel!

facts: Squirrels bury nuts for later — the forgotten ones can grow into new trees!
A squirrel’s bushy tail is a blanket and helps it balance.

wolf.name: Luna the Wolf
wolf.home: forests of North America and Europe

activity.morning: Luna and the pack wake up together. Lick, sniff — good morning, family!
activity.afternoon: The wolf pups play tag in the grass while Luna watches.
activity.evening: Under the moon, Luna howls to call the family home. Ahoooo! Goodnight, Luna!

facts: Wolves howl to talk to their family, even far away.
Wolves live in families called packs.

kiwi.name: Kiri the Kiwi

activity.morning: Shhh… Kiri is fast asleep in a cozy burrow. Many kiwis rest in the daytime and search for food at night.
activity.afternoon: Still sleeping… snore… Kiri is saving energy for tonight.
activity.evening: Night time! Kiri wakes up and sniffs the ground with a long beak to find wiggly worms. Good morning… I mean, goodnight, Kiri!

facts: Kiwis have nostrils at the very tip of their beak!
A kiwi is a bird that can’t fly.

fennec.name: Fen the Fennec Fox

activity.morning: Fen sleeps in a cool burrow under the sand, away from the hot sun.
activity.afternoon: The desert is SO hot. Fen stays underground and waits.
activity.evening: The desert cools down. Fen’s giant ears listen for little bugs. Goodnight, Fen!

facts: Fennec foxes have very large ears for their size — they help them stay cool!
Fennec foxes have furry feet so the hot sand doesn’t burn them.

hedgehog.name: Nico the Hedgehog

activity.morning: Nico is asleep in a pile of soft leaves. Zzz…
activity.afternoon: Still asleep… Hedgehogs are mostly active after dark.
activity.evening: Snuffle, snuffle! Nico looks for beetles in the garden. A noise! Nico rolls into a spiky ball. Goodnight, Nico!

facts: A hedgehog has thousands of spines on its back!
When scared, a hedgehog rolls into a spiky ball.

nessie.name: Nessie of the Loch
nessie.home: Loch Ness, a big lake in Scotland

activity.morning: Mist floats on the lake. People wait with cameras. Is that a long neck in the water? Or just a log?
activity.afternoon: A big ripple goes across the lake… then nothing. Nessie is very, very shy!
activity.evening: The lake is quiet and dark. Maybe Nessie is swimming deep down, dreaming. Goodnight, Nessie!

facts: Loch Ness is a very big, very deep lake in Scotland.
People have looked for Nessie for many years, but there is no scientific proof she exists!

yeti.name: Yeti of the Mountains

activity.morning: High in the snowy mountains, climbers find giant footprints. Whose feet are SO big?
activity.afternoon: The wind blows. Something fluffy and white runs behind a rock… or was it just snow?
activity.evening: The stars shine on the tallest mountains in the world. Goodnight, Yeti, wherever you are!

facts: The Himalayas have the tallest mountains in the world, like Mount Everest.
Scientists tested some “Yeti” hair — it came from bears!

bigfoot.name: Bigfoot

activity.morning: In the big forest, a hiker finds a HUGE footprint in the mud. Stomp!
activity.afternoon: Something tall and hairy walks between the trees… Is it Bigfoot? Or a bear?
activity.evening: The forest is quiet. Maybe Bigfoot is having a big, hairy nap. Goodnight, Bigfoot!

facts: Bigfoot is also called Sasquatch.
Nobody has ever proven Bigfoot is real, but people still love to look!

naga.name: Naga of the Mekong
naga.home: the Mekong River in Thailand and Laos

activity.morning: The great Mekong River sparkles in the sun. People say a giant serpent lives deep below.
activity.afternoon: Fishermen tell stories of the Naga, who protects the river and its fish.
activity.evening: Some people report seeing mysterious lights near the river on special nights. In the legend, they say: “The Naga is sending fireballs!” Goodnight, Naga!

facts: In Thailand and Laos, people tell stories of the Naga, a great serpent of the Mekong River.
Every year, crowds gather by the Mekong to watch for “Naga fireballs”.

jackalope.name: Jackie the Jackalope

activity.morning: A little rabbit hops in the grass… wait, does it have ANTLERS?
activity.afternoon: Boing! Jackie jumps over a cactus. Nobody can catch a jackalope!
activity.evening: Jackie hides in the tall grass, antlers and all. Goodnight, Jackie!

facts: The jackalope is a funny legend: a rabbit with deer antlers!
In Douglas, Wyoming, there is a giant jackalope statue!
